newsitem.title: USA: Troy, NY, rejects mayor's refinancing plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Troy, NY, rejects mayor's refinancing plan - paper.

text.p: The City Council for Troy, N.Y., which a rating agency has said is at risk of default, has rejected part of the mayor's refinancing plan, jeopardizing a new bond issue, the Troy Record said.

Troy, which faces a substantial debt burden, has said it does not have the money for a $1.4 million payment on $35 million of debt that is due on September 15. Even if the bondholders agree to extend the deadline, Moody's Investors Service has said it would consider that a default.

In its Friday edition, the paper said the rejected bill would have authorized the city to borrow $6 million to create a debt reserve and to pay for the costs of issuing new bonds through the Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC).
The MAC was imposed by the state in 1995 because Troy could not sell its debt on its own.
Mayor Mark Pattison said he planned to call a special meeting next week to reintroduce the measure, which he estimates would save the city $800,000 a year, the paper said.

However the council did approve two refinancings. One would let Troy exchange $16.6 million in short-term notes loaned by the state comptroller for long-term bonds at a lower interest rate. The city estimated this would save $500,000 each year over the next 20 years, the Troy Record said.
The other measure would save Troy about $300,000 a year by halving the payments on a $5.2 million loan for building the Knickerbacker Arena in 1990.
